title: Secondary candidates and benchmark shelf
status: Reported baseline collected · no investment conclusion
purpose: This is the evidence-backed waiting room around the four core companies. Secondary candidates can earn a core seat only through repeated commercial and economic proof. Benchmarks help interpret the wider infrastructure landscape, but are not being promoted as current thesis candidates or expectation-gap calls.

secondary.name: Zscaler
secondary.question: Can security for enterprise agents become a paid, durable control plane rather than a feature set embedded in the existing platform?

reportedBaseline.label: Q4 free cash flow
reportedBaseline.note: Affected by $218.5M of capex and internal-use software

secondary.mechanism: More autonomous access to applications, data, and tools could create additional policy, data-protection, and agent-security control points. The relevant billable outcome is paid platform adoption or non-seat-based security spend—not simply more AI traffic.

tests.title: Make agent security commercially visible
tests.upgrade: Management discloses paid adoption, customer scale, attach, pricing, transaction volume, or revenue contribution for security-for-agents capabilities.
tests.notEnough: An agent-security launch, framework support, or generic platform commentary without a commercial measure.
tests.downgrade: The capabilities appear bundled, experimental, or commercially immaterial across repeated reports.

tests.title: Keep the ARR read comparable
tests.upgrade: Organic ARR, net-new ARR, and non-seat-based solutions sustain quality after separating acquisition effects.
tests.notEnough: Reported ARR growth without clear acquisition and organic comparability.
tests.downgrade: Organic growth weakens while acquisitions or price changes obscure the underlying demand signal.

tests.title: Protect cash conversion
tests.upgrade: Capacity investment supports durable growth while free-cash-flow margin returns toward the guided profile.
tests.notEnough: Strong operating cash flow without evidence of the full capital burden.
tests.downgrade: Investment remains elevated and cash economics deteriorate without an identifiable paid agent-security return.

secondary.boundary: Zscaler’s own AI-security research can support a macro control-demand proxy, but it is not proof of Zscaler agent-specific revenue. Red Canary also makes reported ARR comparability a continuing requirement.

sources.label: Zscaler Q4 FY2026 results and FY2027 outlook

secondary.name: Twilio
secondary.question: Can agent-driven customer and business interactions increase paid communications and engagement use without eroding the economics of the carrier-heavy delivery layer?
secondary.mechanism: An agent that chats, calls, verifies, or follows up creates billable communications and engagement events. The economic test is whether incremental event volume carries attractive gross margin, retention, and cash conversion.

tests.title: Show paid agent-driven activity
tests.upgrade: The company discloses agent-related message, voice, engagement, customer, revenue, pricing, or retention evidence tied to a paid product.
tests.notEnough: A platform or Agent Connect launch without volume, pricing, customer, or gross-profit evidence.
tests.downgrade: Agent features are bundled or immaterial and the relevant usage categories do not gain commercial traction.

tests.title: Keep organic expansion durable
tests.upgrade: Organic growth and dollar-based net expansion remain healthy across comparable customer cohorts.
tests.notEnough: Reported growth without the organic comparison or a durable cohort read.
tests.downgrade: Organic growth or expansion weakens despite a stronger AI communications narrative.

tests.title: Convert activity into profitable cash flow
tests.upgrade: Gross margin, operating income, and free cash flow show that higher event volume is economically productive.
tests.notEnough: More revenue without visibility into carrier costs, mix, margin, and cash conversion.
tests.downgrade: Usage grows but carrier costs or mix pressure compress the incremental economics.

secondary.boundary: Twilio does not separately disclose agent-driven communications, revenue, pricing, or retention. General platform growth does not establish the proposed agentic mechanism.

sources.label: Twilio next-generation platform and Agent Connect

secondary.name: Fastly
secondary.question: Can machine-heavy traffic translate into durable, paid edge delivery and security consumption with a materially better cash outcome?

reportedBaseline.label: Q2 free cash flow
reportedBaseline.note: Operating cash flow was $39.3M; cash conversion remains a key test

secondary.mechanism: More machine retrieval, inference-adjacent requests, and AI application delivery can expand usage of edge delivery, security, compute, and observability. The shareholder test is recurring customer economics and cash, not a traffic statistic alone.

tests.title: Connect traffic to paid adoption
tests.upgrade: The company identifies paid AI-delivery, AI-firewall, compute, security, or observability adoption with customer, usage, price, or revenue evidence.
tests.notEnough: A statement that machine traffic is large or growing faster than human traffic.
tests.downgrade: Machine-traffic relevance grows while paid adoption and disclosed revenue linkage remain absent.

tests.title: Make growth recurring and diversified
tests.upgrade: RPO, net retention, and product-category growth remain strong without increasing customer concentration.
tests.notEnough: One quarter of top-line growth without a durable retention or concentration read.
tests.downgrade: Retention weakens, commitments slow, or a small group of customers drives the result.

tests.title: Turn activity into cash
tests.upgrade: Gross-margin and free-cash-flow evidence improves as growth scales.
tests.notEnough: Higher operating cash flow while free cash flow remains de minimis.
tests.downgrade: Network, capex, or operating costs prevent meaningful cash conversion.

secondary.boundary: Fastly’s network research is useful machine-activity context, not company-capture proof. The first baseline also includes 37% of revenue from its ten largest customers, so concentration stays visible.

sources.label: Fastly AI Firewall and AI Runtime Control update

secondary.name: Okta
secondary.question: Can delegated agent identity and authorization become a paid extension of the identity platform rather than an important but bundled security capability?
secondary.mechanism: Agents acting on behalf of users or systems need identity, access policy, delegated authority, and auditability. The economic test is an incremental paid identity workload, not merely a broader identity threat surface.

tests.title: Make agent identity paid and measurable
tests.upgrade: Management discloses paid agent-identity customers, attach, pricing, identity transactions, revenue, or retention tied to the capability.
tests.notEnough: An AI-agent security blueprint, ecosystem integration, beta, or architectural announcement.
tests.downgrade: Agent identity remains a free control, partner feature, or non-material roadmap item across repeated reports.

tests.title: Keep the demand signal intact
tests.upgrade: Subscription revenue, RPO / cRPO, and guidance continue to support durable identity-platform demand.
tests.notEnough: A single RPO improvement without comparable subscription and current-RPO evidence.
tests.downgrade: Growth or commitment momentum weakens while the agent identity opportunity stays unquantified.

tests.title: Preserve the return profile
tests.upgrade: Operating and free-cash-flow margins hold while the company invests in the new workload.
tests.notEnough: A relevant product narrative without a margin or cash outcome.
tests.downgrade: Investment or mix pressure erodes returns without an identifiable commercial benefit.

secondary.boundary: Okta does not separately disclose agent-identity revenue, price, customer count, or attach. Professional-services partner changes also affect reported growth comparability and should not be mistaken for product demand.

sources.label: Okta Q2 FY2027 results and outlook

benchmarks.name: Cloudflare
benchmarks.lens: Integrated edge, developer, security, and agent infrastructure
benchmarks.whyBenchmark: A broad reference point for how edge delivery, AI controls, developer tools, identity, and agent payments could converge on one network. It helps frame the competitive ceiling for several candidates.
benchmarks.whatWouldChangeRole: Move from benchmark to a formal candidate only after its own billable mechanism, economics, and expectation-gap evidence are researched under the same gates.
benchmarks.boundary: This is not a valuation or investment view. Relevant products and high growth do not tell us what is already expected or whether agent infrastructure is the reason for the result.

sources.label: Cloudflare agent identity and wallet update

benchmarks.name: Datadog
benchmarks.whyBenchmark: A quality reference for whether AI-enabled monitoring, security, and autonomous remediation can be carried by a software and cash-flow model at scale.
benchmarks.whatWouldChangeRole: Move from benchmark to a formal candidate only after the project writes a named billable-agent mechanism, repeated commercial evidence, and expectations history.
benchmarks.boundary: AI product activity and fast growth are not agent-specific revenue disclosure. No company-specific expectation-gap conclusion has been made.

benchmarks.name: Palo Alto Networks
benchmarks.whyBenchmark: A scale reference for how a broad security platform may absorb new agent-control workloads, and a reminder that platform consolidation can limit standalone monetization for smaller control-plane candidates.
benchmarks.whatWouldChangeRole: Move from benchmark to a formal candidate only after its agent-specific pricing, demand, economics, and expectations evidence are evaluated independently.
benchmarks.boundary: Acquisitions, integration, and a broad product base complicate causal attribution. The project does not infer agent-specific capture from aggregate platform metrics.

sources.label: Palo Alto Networks Q4 and FY2026 results

promotionProtocol.title: Two comparable reports
promotionProtocol.detail: Record at least two company-reported periods under a stable definition before claiming a direction of travel.

promotionProtocol.title: Commercial proof
promotionProtocol.detail: Require a paid adoption, price, usage-to-revenue, attach, retention, margin, or cash outcome linked to the proposed mechanism.

promotionProtocol.title: Counterargument survives
promotionProtocol.detail: Keep acquisition effects, customer concentration, cost-to-serve, bundling, and alternate growth drivers visible.

promotionProtocol.title: Only then assess the gap
promotionProtocol.detail: Add fiscal-aligned, point-in-time consensus and valuation history before saying the market may not have priced the evidence.
